speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This event has important implications for all Singaporeans beyond the residents that are affected, but the media and Government have downplayed these implications.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Therefore, I will be using my Adjournment Motion speech today to explain to Singaporeans why they should be concerned about the Ang Mo Kio SERS and how it will affect the future of their ageing HDB flats.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Some Singaporeans may not fully understand how and why the Ang Mo Kio SERS is different from other SERS exercises in the past.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I will first explain briefly how Ang Mo Kio SERS is different from past SERS.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: An equivalent flat is defined as one that is the same flat-type, same size and located at a designated site near the current site.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I confirmed this during the deliberations of the Public Petitions Committee, where I persistently asked the Ministry of National Development (MND) for past examples of SERS where the residents had needed to top up with cash for an equivalent flat with a new 99-year lease.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Only residents who opted for "a more centrally located replacement site" at Clementi Avenue 1 were required to top up with cash.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Thus, the Government's example of West Coast Road SERS cannot be taken as an example of past SERS residents having to top up cash for an equivalent flat.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This confirms that the Ang Mo Kio residents are the unlucky first SERS residents to be financially burdened.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: For the first time, residents of a SERS must fork out cash for an equivalent flat with a new 99-year lease.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The Government has repeatedly stated it has used the same model and approach as other SERS to compute the compensation for the Ang Mo Kio SERS, but the Government has not admitted that the outcome of the Ang Mo Kio SERS is different from other SERS.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It is disingenuous of the Government to have not admitted to the different outcome up till today, even though the outcome is undeniably different.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If the outcome was not different, there would have been no need for the Government to introduce the 50-year lease and Lease Buyback Scheme (LBS) as new options for the Ang Mo Kio residents.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Short of admitting the different outcome, Minister Desmond Lee had tried to give the reason for the different outcome in his response to Ang Mo Kio Member Ms Nadia Samdin's Adjournment Motion speech in July 2022.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The Minister explained that in past SERS, the flats were generally younger at the point of the SERS announcement, with around 70 years of lease remaining.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: However, the flats affected by the Ang Mo Kio SERS are older, with a lease balance of about 57 years.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In my opinion, the full explanation is that lease decay has affected prices of old HDB flats in mature estates more than the ones in non-mature estates.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: At the same time, the prices of new flats in mature estates have risen much faster because they enjoy the benefits of good amenities and location.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Therefore, there is a larger price difference between the existing old flats and the new replacement flats in Ang Mo Kio than in Marsiling.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This is the key reason why the Ang Mo Kio residents have suffered a worse outcome than that of the residents of the Marsiling SERS and previous SERS exercises when the effect of lease decay had not set in.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The Government should have admitted to the different outcome and offered this full explanation to the Ang Mo Kio residents upfront.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, what is the reason that the Government has avoided admitting the different outcome and, as a result of that, is unable to provide a full explanation to the Ang Mo Kio residents and Singaporeans?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I think the reason is, by admitting to the different outcome of the Ang Mo Kio SERS, it means the Voluntary Early Redevelopment Scheme, or VERS, is not a viable solution to the lease decay problem.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Since 2018, the Government, however, has touted VERS as a solution to the lease decay problem.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Singaporeans are expecting VERS to be like "SERS for all".

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: But it is a different story if VERS is actually "Ang Mo Kio SERS for all".

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The original SERS means residents get paid; while the Ang Mo Kio SERS means residents must pay.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Since the market-based compensation formula that the Government had used for SERS all this while has failed to enable Ang Mo Kio residents to exchange their 42-year-old flats for new ones without having to top-up cash, VERS cannot be a solution to the lease decay problem, as the flats under VERS will be even older, at more than 70 years old.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This will be especially true if the price disparity between the new and older flats in mature estates which we see today, continues to persist.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If the Government uses the same formula as SERS to compensate VERS residents, it is certain that the VERS resident will have to pay a lot more cash or move to a cheaper area with the proceeds from VERS.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The likelihood of any VERS proposal being approved will also be nil, because Singaporeans have come to associate "en bloc" with windfalls and new homes, and the redevelopment of mature estates envisioned by VERS will not materialise.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: VERS will be doomed if the Government uses the same compensation formula as it did for the Ang Mo Kio SERS.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: By not admitting to the different outcome of the Ang Mo Kio SERS and the financial plight of the Ang Mo Kio residents, the Government continues to keep silent on the non-viability of VERS.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The right thing to do, however, is to clarify to Singaporeans whether it would be devising a new compensation formula for VERS or proposing some other solutions for the lease decay problem, which has serious implications on the financial well-being and retirement plans of Singaporeans, especially those who bought older flats in the mature estates before the lease decay issue was thrown into the spotlight.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Even though the Government has followed the same model and approach, as a government responsible to the people, it should have thought through the implications of the different compensations and come out with more palatable solutions beforehand.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Had the Ang Mo Kio SERS residents not protested, this issue would not have been drawn into the national spotlight and we would not be able to assess its implications for SERS in future.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Singaporeans deserve better – for country, for people.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: He has raised some issues again and I would like to take this opportunity to recap what has transpired in the case of the Ang Mo Kio SERS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: It has not been pegged or designed this way, although in his speech, Mr Leong has sought to make it so.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: How does it come about that a flat that has, say, 70 years left on its lease can be worth more than a similar flat, in terms of size and location, with a full 99 years to run?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is largely because the new flat on a 99-year lease comes with Government subsidies, which are so substantive that after netting off some additional financial support from the SERS grant and the payment of reasonable expenses by HDB, eligible buyers can actually pay less than what a similar flat with 70 years left would fetch on the resale market.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: During earlier SERS exercises, the flats that were acquired were generally younger, such that most unit owners would be able to afford a subsidised replacement flat of similar attributes on a fresh 99-year lease.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The compensation framework was based on independent assessment, which, in turn, was based on market value.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: It was not pegged to the subsidised price of new flats, nor designed to create a windfall.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: It so happened, during past SERS exercises, that the outcome was quite advantageous for most flat owners, because the age of their flats was not so old.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: A different outcome would occur if the age of the flats involved in SERS were older.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Because a flat with, say, 57 years left, would fetch a lower value on the resale market than one with 70 years left.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: And this was what happened in the case of the Ang Mo Kio SERS exercise; and would, in fact, be the case in future SERS exercises if the flats involved are of similar vintage.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: First, the Government has maintained consistency in our approach with previous exercises.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is quite in contrast with the picture that Mr Leong was trying to paint, which is that somehow, an epochal moment was made possible without the Government admitting so.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I am afraid Mr Leong is painting quite an incorrect picture here.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In addition, the Government also listened to the residents and once we heard their key concerns, we introduced flexibility to meet their needs by offering more options, such as the 50-year leases, as well as the LBS for seniors and allowing flexibility for the residents to apply for a site that is different than the original designated replacement site at Central Weave at Ang Mo Kio.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: So, we reject the characterisation of a lack of empathy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We have been walking the ground and we have also been listening to residents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I feel that we need to repeat this: 99% of the flat owners who were involved in the Ang Mo Kio SERS exercise do not need to top-up to purchase a similar type of flat with a full 99-year lease or a similar size flat on a 50-year lease.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: So, the Government, in determining the compensation for SERS flats has been consistent in applying valuation principles that are well-established.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In addition, we have been giving our SERS households considerable support.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: All these have been enumerated in our public communications and I feel that it is not necessary for us to repeat that here.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Leong then goes on to characterise what has happened in the Ang Mo Kio SERS case as one that is due to an effect of diminishing leases and then to use that to shape certain expectations of the public of the VERS scheme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I feel that it is important for us to make very clear here.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I have explained why residents need to top up when they swop a 57-year lease for a new 99-year lease.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This was also made clear during our public communications with our residents in Ang Mo Kio, as well as in response to the public Petition.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: And I believe that Mr Leong acknowledges that.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: However, it seems that he does not prefer this outcome.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: That does not make it an unfair one.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: SERS is not meant to extend a decaying lease for free to 99 years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: That is not the basis upon which SERS compensation is determined.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: It is determined by a fair, independent assessment and that, in turn, takes reference from market value.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: VERS, like SERS, is not meant to extend a diminishing lease for free to 99 years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The alternative to SERS or VERS is for the residents to stay in place until their lease runs out, at which point they would have to find a new flat on a new lease.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: So, I believe what Mr Leong is doing here, is to shape certain ungrounded expectations of VERS which are at odds with what we have shared so far.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: So, if we examine what Mr Leong has been doing, I think he has been reshaping people's expectations of the scheme and I cannot help but wonder why he is doing so.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Be that as it may, it does not seem very inconsistent with what Mr Leong has been doing because, as I have explained, the SERS scheme compensation was not designed for flat owners to be able to purchase a same size flat on a fresh 99-year lease in a very similar location.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: But Mr Leong has painted it as the objective.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We can understand in the case of SERS that residents or flat owners may hope for more compensation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We can understand if they have formed these expectations based on the experiences of previous flat owners who have gone through the SERS exercises.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: And I can only wonder at his purpose for doing this, Mr Speaker.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I am mindful that Mr Leong has been making various arguments – in our opinion, erroneous arguments – outside of the House with regard to the valuation and the pricing of Build-To-Order (BTO) flats and also, by extension, the proper use of national Reserves.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To do otherwise makes it harder, not easier, for us collectively to balance the needs of Singaporeans, and I am talking about the current generation as well as the future generations.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Speaker, I thank the Senior Minister of State for responding to my speech.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: However, contrary to what the Senior Minister of State has said, I think the Government has actually shaped certain expectations in our society already.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: I am not the one who is reshaping the expectations.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: For example, SERS, for all the past SERS exercises, the residents had received cash and gotten an equivalent flat with a 99-year lease.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Is that not an expectation cultivated by the Government?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: I am just saying the Ang Mo Kio SERS residents have a totally different package and Government, please admit to it.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: That is the first communication that you have to be frank with the Ang Mo Kio residents.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: And I am not necessarily — So, I would like to the Senior Minister of State to clarify.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Even after I have shared the reasons why I think the Ang Mo Kio SERS package is totally different from the packages of the past SERS, does she still think that that is a wrong claim?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: The second question is, does she think again the expectation on VERS is not my shaping the expectations in our society.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: The Government has given the expectations, first of all, that HDB flats are an appreciating asset.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Mr Leong, can you keep your clarification succinct, please?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Yes, and as an answer to the lease decay, the Government has suggested VERS.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: So, how have we not been shaping the expectations and putting out information in a transparent way?

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: So, Mr Speaker, I think that what Mr Leong is trying to do, once again, is to confuse the public.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: I believe that the information that we have been putting out is transparent and we also have been consistent in doing so.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: So, Mr Speaker, I think what Mr Leong is trying to do here is something that is increasingly evident to everyone.
